'''Chapter 1195''' is titled "Weakness".

==Cover Page==
[[Cover Page]] Request: "[[Sanji]] the stylist giving a horse's mane a trim" by PN Hebo (Eiichiro Kakuta).

==Short Summary==
Having been completely outmatched by [[Roronoa Zoro|Zoro]], [[Shepherd Sommers|Sommers]] attempts to flee but is struck down by Zoro's [[Haki/Supreme King Haki|Supreme King Haki]]-infused attack. At the branch route, [[Brook]] confronts [[Manmayer Gunko|Gunko]] to confirm her identity as Princess Shuri, while Gunko's repressed memories and the [[Covenant]] struggle over her body. At the [[Owl Library]], [[Nico Robin|Robin]] and [[Jaguar D. Saul|Saul]] open the ancient chest, which contains an item related to [[Nefertari D. Lili]] who once lived in [[Elbaph]]. At the Western Village, [[Sanji]] is overwhelmed by [[Rimoshifu Killingham|Killingham]]'s [[immortality]]. As Sanji recalls [[Scopper Gaban|Gaban]]'s advice to awaken his Supreme King Haki by not devaluving himself, his repressed memories during his stay at [[Momoiro Island]] suddenly emerge.

==Long Summary==
Overwhelmed with fear now that [[Roronoa Zoro|Zoro]] has properly mastered his [[Haki/Supreme King Haki|Supreme King Haki]], [[Shepherd Sommers|Sommers]] begins fleeing for his life, which annoys Zoro after all the time and energy he spent trying to reach this level of power. As such, Zoro pursues Sommers, who desperately begs him to stay away, but Zoro catches up to Sommers easily and strikes him down on one of the tree branches.

Back with [[Brook|Brook's]] group, [[Manmayer Gunko|Gunko]] stands up on her own as Brook promises not to hurt her, while the other [[Straw Hat Pirates|Straw Hats]] stand by in case she tries to attack. Brook asks Gunko to introduce herself, and she remembers Brook when he was alive, the day [[Reuven]] was killed, and interestingly, begging [[Nerona Imu|Imu]] to let her live. The strain of these seemingly repressed memories causes Gunko to fall to her knees, which Brook takes as a sign that she truly is not an enemy if she is hesitating compared to her first encounter with everyone. Brook says to Gunko that while he swore he would not forgive her for that fateful day, if she had no free will of her own, then he believes she was the one who suffered the most. Gunko begins to cry, which Jinbe notices, and Brook tells her to take her time, as he knows a few words are not enough to explain all these years. Therefore, Brook offers to introduce himself first, and after he does, he asks her if she truly is Shuri. Gunko remembers Imu ordering her and [[Figarland Shamrock|Shamrock]] to subjugate [[Elbaph]] as their battle-slaves, and while gripping her arm, which has the [[Covenant|Depths Covenant]], Gunko tearfully affirms herself as a [[World Noble]] of the [[Manmayer Family]], leaving Brook shocked. Brook then asks why Gunko is crying and he begins to sing "[[We're All Bones When We Die]]", but Gunko creates a sword made of her [[Aro Aro no Mi|arrows]] and fires a blast at Brook demanding he stay away from her. Brook sees her stance and reminds her he taught her that stance, but Gunko insists she does not know Brook and starts running away, while Brook calls to her. 

At the [[Owl Library]], the box is opened and [[Jaguar D. Saul|Saul]] asks if what is inside is truly needed now. [[Biblo]], translated through [[Tony Tony Chopper|Chopper]], tells the three of them that long ago, a human named "[[Nefertari D. Lili|Lili]]" lived on Elbaph, a name that catches [[Nico Robin|Robin's]] attention. At the Western Village, the giants only have four children left to save; [[Colon]], [[Ylva]], [[Bjorn]], and [[Johanna]], as [[Rimoshifu Killingham|Killingham]] orders his [[Zaza]] [[MMA]] to reach the port where he assumes Sommers still is. Despite his injuries, [[Sanji]] flies at him annoyed he would be so arrogant to assume he has won as he unleashes an attack called ''Ifrit Jambe: Sky Table Kick Course'', splitting Killingham in half before shredding him to bits. Killingham easily reforms as he reminds Sanji that no matter how many times he attacks the outcome is the same, and he will never have Supreme King Haki, labeling him an insect that has reached the limit of his capabilities. Killingham returns to his hybrid form and fires a beam of energy from [[Longinus]] that pierces Sanji's side, causing him to fall to the ground. Killingham stands over him, where he admits he is impressed Sanji is so sturdy to withstand the power of Longinus, as Sanji thinks back to what [[Scopper Gaban|Gaban]] said to him about his habit of self-sabotage, despite Sanji never perceiving his self-sacrificial behavior in the past as such. Killingham then stabs Sanji in the arm as he mockingly asks him what exactly commonfolk eat since Sanji called himself a chef earlier, but rather than react to the pain, Sanji starts reopening memories from the past that he desperately wants to keep locked away. 

It turns out said memories are from during his time training on [[Momoiro Island]], when [[Emporio Ivankov|Ivankov]] started singing to Sanji that he suffers from a crippling weakness.

==Trivia==
*Sanji's flashbacks at the end of the chapter are callbacks to previous scenes from the manga, some of which were either redesigned or shown from a new angle:
*#Redesigned scene from [[Chapter 59]], as Luffy scolds him, now seen from over Sanji's shoulder.
*#Redesigned panel from [[Chapter 284]], after saving [[Usopp]] from [[Enel]], now seen from a little further away.
*#Redesigned scene from [[Chapter 485]], while trying to convince [[Bartholomew Kuma|Kuma]] to take him over Luffy or Zoro, now seen with Sanji's face.
*#Redesigned scene from [[Chapter 813]], after throwing the rest of the Curly Hat Pirates out of [[Capone Bege|Bege]], now seen with Sanji's face.
*#Scene from [[Chapter 852]], while talking to [[Vinsmoke Reiju|Reiju]].
